speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In contrast, checking and savings accounts at commercial banks are liabilities of the banks, not the Federal Reserve.
rationale: Describes the existing monetary system without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The bulk of transactions, by value, that U.S. households and firms make each day use commercial bank money as the payment instrument.
rationale: Describes current payment system usage without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Federal Reserve Accounts and Commercial Bank Accounts Under current law, the Federal Reserve offers accounts and payment services to commercial banks.
rationale: Describes current Federal Reserve account services to banks without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: These accounts provide a risk-free settlement asset for trillions of dollars of daily interbank payments.
rationale: Describes the current function of Fed accounts for banks, not a CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Importantly, the use of central bank money to settle interbank payments promotes financial stability because it eliminates credit and liquidity risk in systemically important payment systems.
rationale: Describes the macro role of central bank money in interbank settlement without naming any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Congress did not establish the Federal Reserve to provide accounts directly to the general public; the Federal Reserve instead works in the background by providing accounts to commercial banks, which then provide bank accounts to the general public.
rationale: Describes the intermediated/two-tier model where the Fed works through commercial banks rather than providing direct public access, which limits CBDC's threat to deposits.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Under this structure, commercial banks act as an intermediary between the Federal Reserve and the general public.
rationale: Describes the intermediated/two-tier model where commercial banks stand between the Fed and the public, a protective design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The funds in commercial bank accounts are digital and can be used to make digital payments to households and businesses, but commercial banks promise to redeem a dollar in one's bank account into $1 of U.S. currency.
rationale: Describes the existing commercial banking system's convertibility feature, not a CBDC design parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In short, banks peg the exchange rate between commercial bank money and the U.S. dollar at one-to-one.
rationale: Describes the existing commercial bank money system, not a CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Due to substantial regulatory and supervisory oversight and federal deposit insurance, households and firms reasonably view this fixed exchange rate as perfectly credible.
rationale: Describes the current banking system's credibility mechanisms without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Consequently, they treat commercial bank money and central bank money as perfect substitutes—they are interchangeable as a means of payment.
rationale: Describes the current state of money substitutability without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The credibility of this fixed exchange rate between commercial and central bank money is what allows our payment system to be stable and efficient.
rationale: Discusses the general principle of fixed exchange rate credibility in the payment system without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I will return to this point later.
rationale: This is a transitional sentence with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This division of functions between the Federal Reserve and commercial banks reflects an economic truth: that markets operate efficiently when private-sector firms compete to provide the highest-quality products to consumers and businesses at the lowest possible cost.
rationale: Discusses general economic principle about public-private division of labor, not a specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In general, the government should compete with the private sector only to address market failures.
rationale: General principle about government-private sector roles with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Consideration of the Case for a Federal Reserve CBDC This brings us back to my original question: What is the problem with our current payment system that only a CBDC would solve?
rationale: The sentence poses a general question about CBDC motivation and problem-solving without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be that physical currency will disappear?
rationale: Sentence poses a question about currency disappearance as a motivation for CBDC, not a concrete design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: As I mentioned before, the key to having credible commercial bank money is the promise that banks will convert a dollar of digital bank money into a dollar of U.S. physical currency.
rationale: Convertibility of bank deposits into physical currency is presented as a safeguard that protects the credibility of commercial bank money.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: But how can banks deliver on their promise if U.S. currency disappears?
rationale: Discusses the motivation for CBDC (cashless economy concern) without naming any specific design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Accordingly, many central banks are considering adoption of a CBDC as their economies become "cashless."
rationale: Discusses CBDC adoption motivation in cashless economies without naming any specific design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Eliminating currency is a policy choice, however, not an economic outcome, and Chair Powell has made clear that U.S. currency is not going to be replaced by a CBDC.
rationale: The sentence discusses policy stance on currency replacement, not a specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Thus, a fear of imminently vanishing physical currency cannot be the reason for adopting a CBDC.
rationale: The sentence discusses motivation for CBDC adoption without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be that the payment system is too limited in reach, and that introducing a CBDC would make the payment system bigger, broader, and more efficient?
rationale: Discusses motivation for CBDC (payment system reach and efficiency) without naming any concrete design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It certainly doesn't look that way to me.
rationale: This is a general evaluative statement about CBDC necessity without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Our existing interbank payment services have nationwide reach, meaning that an accountholder at one commercial bank can make a payment to an accountholder at any other U.S. bank.
rationale: Describes existing interbank payment infrastructure without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The same applies to international payments—accountholders at U.S. banks can transfer funds abroad to accountholders at foreign banks.
rationale: Describes existing payment system capabilities without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: So, a lack of connectedness and geographic breadth in the U.S. payment system is not a good reason to introduce a CBDC.
rationale: Discusses motivation against CBDC issuance without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be that existing payment services are too slow?
rationale: The sentence questions payment speed as a CBDC motivation without naming any concrete design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: A group of commercial banks has recently developed an instant payment service (the Real-Time Payment Service, or RTP), and the Federal Reserve is creating its own instant payment service, FedNowSM.
rationale: Describes existing/planned private and Fed payment services, not CBDC design features.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: These services will move funds between accountholders at U.S. commercial banks immediately after a payment is initiated.
rationale: Describes existing instant payment services between commercial bank accounts, not a CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: While cross-border payments are typically less efficient than domestic payments, efforts are underway to improve cross-border payments as well.
rationale: Discusses cross-border payment efficiency generally without naming any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: These innovations are all moving forward in the absence of a CBDC.
rationale: Discusses CBDC necessity in general without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Consequently, facilitating speedier payments is not a compelling reason to create a CBDC.
rationale: This sentence argues against CBDC issuance based on payment speed but does not mention any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be that too few people can access the payment system?
rationale: This is a motivational question about access to the payment system in general, not a concrete CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Some argue that introducing a CBDC would improve financial inclusion by allowing the unbanked to more readily access financial services.
rationale: Describes broad access as a possibility without endorsing it as limiting or expanding deposit substitution.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: To address this argument, we need to know, first, the size of the unbanked population, and second, whether the unbanked population would use a Federal Reserve CBDC account.
rationale: The sentence poses questions about the unbanked population without discussing any concrete CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: According to a recent Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) survey, approximately 5.4 percent of U.S. households were unbanked in 2019.
rationale: The sentence provides a statistic about the unbanked population without discussing any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The FDIC survey also found that approximately 75 percent of the unbanked population "were not at all interested" or "not very interested" in having a bank account.
rationale: Discusses unbanked population's interest in accounts generally, not a specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: If the same percentage of the unbanked population would not be interested in a Federal Reserve CBDC account, this means that a little more than 1 percent of U.S. households are both unbanked and potentially interested in a Federal Reserve CBDC account.
rationale: The sentence discusses potential adoption/interest levels among the unbanked population, not any concrete CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It is implausible to me that developing a CBDC is the simplest, least costly way to reach this 1 percent of households.
rationale: The sentence expresses skepticism about CBDC as a solution for financial inclusion but does not mention any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Instead, we could promote financial inclusion more efficiently by, for example, encouraging widespread use of low-cost commercial bank accounts through the Cities for Financial Empowerment Bank On project.
rationale: Discusses an alternative to CBDC for financial inclusion without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be that a CBDC is needed because existing payment services are unreasonably expensive?
rationale: The sentence poses a motivational question about CBDC necessity based on payment costs, without naming any concrete design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In order to answer this question, we need to understand why the price charged for a payment might be considered "high."
rationale: The sentence discusses the conceptual framework for evaluating payment prices, not any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In economics, the price of a service is typically composed of two parts: the marginal cost of providing the service and a markup that reflects the market power of the seller.
rationale: This sentence discusses general economics of pricing services, not any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The marginal cost of processing a payment depends on the nature of the payment (for example, paper check versus electronic transfer), the technology used (for example, batched payments versus real-time payments), and the other services provided in processing the payment (for example, risk and fraud services).
rationale: Discusses general payment processing costs and technology factors without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Since these factors are primarily technological, and there is no reason to think that the Federal Reserve can develop cheaper technology than private firms, it seems unlikely that the Federal Reserve would be able to process CBDC payments at a materially lower marginal cost than existing private-sector payment services.
rationale: Discusses cost efficiency of CBDC payment processing without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The key question, then, is how a CBDC would affect the markup charged by banks for a variety of payment services.
rationale: Discusses CBDC's effect on bank pricing/markups without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The markup that a firm can charge depends on its market power and thus the degree of competition it faces.
rationale: General economic principle about market power and competition with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Introducing a CBDC would create additional competition in the market for payment services, because the general public could use CBDC accounts to make payments directly through the Federal Reserve—that is, a CBDC would allow the general public to bypass the commercial banking system.
rationale: Direct Federal Reserve accounts allowing the public to bypass commercial banks makes CBDC a stronger deposit substitute.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Deposits would flow from commercial banks into CBDC accounts, which would put pressure on banks to lower their fees, or raise the interest rate paid on deposits, to prevent additional deposit outflows.
rationale: Describes the competitive effect of CBDC on bank deposits without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It seems to me, however, that private-sector innovations might reduce the markup charged by banks more effectively than a CBDC would.
rationale: Sentence compares CBDC to private-sector innovations in general without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: If commercial banks are earning rents from their market power, then there is a profit opportunity for nonbanks to enter the payment business and provide the general public with cheaper payment services.
rationale: Discusses market competition and nonbank entry as an alternative to CBDC, with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: And, indeed, we are currently seeing a surge of nonbanks getting into payments.
rationale: Describes nonbank entry into payments generally, with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For example, in recent years, "stablecoin" arrangements have emerged as a particularly important type of nonbank entrant into the payments landscape.
rationale: Describes stablecoins as a nonbank payment entrant without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Stablecoins are digital assets whose value is tied to one or more other assets, such as a sovereign currency.
rationale: This sentence defines stablecoins generically without discussing any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: A stablecoin could serve as an attractive payment instrument if it is pegged one-to-one to the dollar and is backed by a safe and liquid pool of assets.
rationale: Describes stablecoin design features, not CBDC design features.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: If one or more stablecoin arrangements can develop a significant user base, they could become a major challenger to banks for processing payments.
rationale: Discusses stablecoins as payment competitors to banks, not a CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Importantly, payments using such stablecoins might be "free" in the sense that there would be no fee required to initiate or receive a payment.
rationale: Discusses stablecoin payment features, not CBDC design parameters.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Accordingly, one can easily imagine that competition from stablecoins could pressure banks to reduce their markup for payment services.
rationale: Discusses competitive pressure from stablecoins on bank payment fees, not a CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Please note that I am not endorsing any particular stablecoin—some of which are not backed by safe and liquid assets.
rationale: Disclaimer about stablecoins with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The promise of redemption of a stablecoin into one U.S. dollar is not perfectly credible, nor have they been tested by an actual run on the stablecoin.
rationale: Discusses stablecoin credibility and run risk without mentioning any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: There are many legal, regulatory, and policy issues that need to be resolved before stablecoins can safely proliferate.
rationale: Discusses general regulatory issues for stablecoins, not a specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: My point, however, is that the private sector is already developing payment alternatives to compete with the banking system.
rationale: Discusses private-sector payment alternatives as CBDC motivation, not a concrete design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Hence, it seems unnecessary for the Federal Reserve to create a CBDC to drive down payment rents.
rationale: Discusses necessity of CBDC issuance generally without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Returning to possible problems a CBDC could solve, it is often argued that the creation of a CBDC would spur innovation in the payment system.
rationale: Discusses CBDC motivation (spurring innovation) without naming any concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This leads me to ask: do we think there is insufficient innovation going on in payments?
rationale: The sentence questions whether CBDC is needed for innovation but names no concrete design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: To the contrary, it seems to me that private-sector innovation is occurring quite rapidly—in fact, faster than regulators can process.
rationale: Discusses pace of private-sector innovation without naming any CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: So, spurring innovation is not a compelling reason to introduce a CBDC.
rationale: Discusses motivation for CBDC issuance without naming any concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be, however, that the types of innovations being pursued by the private sector are the "wrong" types of payment innovations?
rationale: Questions whether private-sector innovation types are appropriate, but names no concrete CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I see some merit in this argument when I consider crypto-assets such as bitcoin that are often used to facilitate illicit activity.
rationale: Discusses crypto-assets and illicit activity without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: But a CBDC is unlikely to deter the use of crypto-assets that are designed to evade governmental oversight.
rationale: Discusses CBDC's general effectiveness against crypto-assets without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could the problem be that government authorities have insufficient information regarding the financial transactions of U.S. citizens?
rationale: The sentence poses a general question about government information access without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In general, the government has sought to balance individuals' right to privacy with the need to prevent illicit financial transactions, such as money laundering.
rationale: Discusses general privacy-illicit finance tradeoff without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For example, while the government does not receive all transaction data regarding accountholders at commercial banks, the Bank Secrecy Act requires that commercial banks report suspicious activity to the government.
rationale: Describes existing bank reporting requirements without naming any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Depending on its design, CBDC accounts could give the Federal Reserve access to a vast amount of information regarding the financial transactions and trading patterns of CBDC accountholders.
rationale: Direct CBDC accounts giving the Fed transaction data implies unintermediated design, making CBDC a stronger deposit substitute.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The introduction of a CBDC in China, for example, likely will allow the Chinese government to more closely monitor the economic activity of its citizens.
rationale: Describes China's CBDC surveillance capability as an example without discussing any specific US CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Should the Federal Reserve create a CBDC for the same reason?
rationale: Rhetorical question about motivation for CBDC issuance with no concrete design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I, for one, do not think so.
rationale: Expresses personal opposition to CBDC issuance without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could the problem be that the reserve currency status of the U.S. dollar is at risk and the creation of a Federal Reserve CBDC is needed to maintain the primacy of the U.S. dollar?
rationale: Discusses motivation for CBDC issuance (reserve currency status) without naming any concrete design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Some commentators have expressed concern, for example, that the availability of a Chinese CBDC will undermine the status of the U.S. dollar.
rationale: Discusses international competition and dollar status motivation without naming any concrete CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I see no reason to expect that the world will flock to a Chinese CBDC or any other.
rationale: Discusses international competition and adoption without naming any concrete CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Why would non-Chinese firms suddenly desire to have all their financial transactions monitored by the Chinese government?
rationale: Mentions monitoring/privacy design feature but as a rhetorical question about adoption barriers, not endorsing a protective or expansive stance.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Why would this induce non-Chinese firms to denominate their contracts and trading activities in the Chinese currency instead of the U.S. dollar?
rationale: The sentence discusses currency denomination and international competition motivations without naming any concrete CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Additionally, I fail to see how allowing U.S. households to, for example, pay their electric bills via a Federal Reserve CBDC account instead of a commercial bank account would help to maintain global dollar supremacy.
rationale: Direct Federal Reserve CBDC accounts for households (unintermediated model) make CBDC a stronger deposit substitute than commercial bank accounts.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: (Of course, Federal Reserve CBDC accounts that are available to persons outside the United States might promote use of the dollar, but global availability of Federal Reserve CBDC accounts would also raise acute problems related to, among other things, money laundering.)
rationale: Global availability of Fed CBDC accounts is an expansive access feature that makes CBDC a stronger deposit substitute internationally.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Finally, could it be that new forms of private money, such as stablecoins, represent a threat to the Federal Reserve for conducting monetary policy?
rationale: The sentence poses a question about stablecoins as a threat to monetary policy, with no concrete CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Many commentators have suggested that new private monies will diminish the impact of the Federal Reserve's policy actions, since they will act as competing monetary systems.
rationale: Discusses general effects of private money on monetary policy without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It is well established in international economics that any country that pegs its exchange rate to the U.S. dollar surrenders its domestic monetary policy to the United States and imports U.S. monetary policy.
rationale: Discusses international monetary policy dynamics with dollar pegs, not a specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This same logic applies to any entity that pegs its exchange rate to the U.S. dollar.
rationale: The sentence discusses monetary policy transmission through dollar pegs in general, with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Consequently, commercial banks and stablecoins pegged to the U.S. dollar act as conduits for U.S. monetary policy and amplify policy actions.
rationale: Discusses monetary policy transmission through dollar-pegged instruments generally, with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: So, if anything, private stablecoins pegged to the dollar broaden the reach of U.S. monetary policy rather than diminish it.
rationale: Discusses stablecoin effects on monetary policy transmission, not any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: After exploring many possible problems that a CBDC could solve, I am left with the conclusion that a CBDC remains a solution in search of a problem.
rationale: This is a general conclusion about CBDC's necessity without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: That leaves us only with more philosophical reasons to adopt a CBDC.
rationale: The sentence discusses philosophical motivations for CBDC adoption without naming any concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: One could argue, for example, that the general public has a fundamental right to hold a riskless digital payment instrument, and a CBDC would do this in a way no privately issued payment instrument can.
rationale: This sentence discusses a philosophical motivation for CBDC (public right to riskless digital instrument) without naming any concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: On the other hand, thanks to federal deposit insurance, commercial bank accounts already offer the general public a riskless digital payment instrument for the vast majority of transactions.
rationale: Discusses existing deposit insurance as a riskless alternative but mentions no specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: One could also argue that the Federal Reserve should provide a digital option as an alternative to the commercial banking system.
rationale: Direct central bank access as an alternative to commercial banks makes CBDC a stronger deposit substitute.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The argument is that the government should not force its citizens to use the commercial banking system, but should instead allow access to the central bank as a public service available to all.
rationale: Direct central bank access as a public alternative to commercial banks makes CBDC a stronger deposit substitute.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: As I noted earlier in my speech, however, the current congressionally mandated division of functions between the Federal Reserve and commercial banks reflects an understanding that, in general, the government should compete with the private sector only to address market failures.
rationale: Discusses general principle of government-private sector roles without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This bedrock principle has stood America in good stead since its founding, and I don't think that CBDCs are the case for making an exception.
rationale: The sentence expresses general skepticism about CBDC as an exception to public-private division, without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In summary, while CBDCs continue to generate enormous interest in the United States and other countries, I remain skeptical that a Federal Reserve CBDC would solve any major problem confronting the U.S. payment system.
rationale: Expresses general skepticism about CBDC solving payment system problems without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: There are also potential costs and risks associated with a CBDC, some of which I have alluded to already.
rationale: General statement about CBDC costs and risks without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I have noted my belief that government interventions into the economy should come only to address significant market failures.
rationale: This sentence expresses a general philosophical view about government intervention without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The competition of a Fed CBDC could disintermediate commercial banks and threaten a division of labor in the financial system that works well.
rationale: Discusses general threat of CBDC to banks without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: And, as cybersecurity concerns mount, a CBDC could become a new target for those threats.
rationale: The sentence discusses cybersecurity risk as a general concern about CBDC, not a specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I expect these and other potential risks from a CBDC will be addressed in the forthcoming discussion paper, and I intend to expand upon them as the debate over digital currencies moves forward.
rationale: Meta-statement about future discussion of risks, no concrete design feature mentioned.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The financial system is undergoing fast-moving changes associated with digitalization and decentralization.
rationale: Describes general trends in the financial system without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Some of these innovations hold considerable promise to reduce transaction costs and frictions, increase competition, and improve financial inclusion, but there are also potential risks.
rationale: General statement about innovation benefits and risks with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: With technology driving profound change, it is important we prepare for the financial system of the future and not limit our thinking to the financial system of today.
rationale: General statement about preparing for future financial systems with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The Evolving Digitalization and Decentralization of Finance In recent years, there has been explosive growth in the development and adoption of new digital assets that leverage distributed ledger technologies and cryptography.
rationale: Describes general trends in digital assets and cryptocurrencies, not a specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The market capitalization of cryptocurrencies grew from less than $100 billion five years ago to a high of almost $3 trillion in November 2021 and is currently around $2 trillion.
rationale: The sentence reports cryptocurrency market capitalization statistics without discussing any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In parallel, we have seen rapid growth in the platforms that facilitate the crypto finance ecosystem, including decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms.
rationale: Describes growth of crypto platforms generally, no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: These crypto platforms facilitate a variety of activities, including lending, trading, and custodying crypto-assets, in some cases outside the traditional regulatory guardrails for investor and consumer protection, market integrity, and transparency.
rationale: Describes crypto platform activities and regulatory gaps, not CBDC design features.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The growth in the crypto finance ecosystem is fueling demand for stablecoins—digital assets that are intended to maintain stable value relative to reference assets, such as the U.S. dollar.
rationale: Describes stablecoin demand growth without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Stablecoin supply grew nearly sixfold in 2021, from roughly $29 billion in January 2021 to $165 billion in January 2022.
rationale: The sentence reports stablecoin market growth statistics without discussing any CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: There is a high degree of concentration among a few dollar-pegged stablecoins: As of January 2022, the largest stablecoin by market capitalization made up almost half of the market, and the four largest stablecoins together made up almost 90 percent.
rationale: Describes stablecoin market concentration with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Today, stablecoins are being used as collateral on DeFi and other crypto platforms, as well as in facilitating trading and monetization of cryptocurrency positions on and between crypto and other platforms.
rationale: Describes current stablecoin uses without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In the future, some issuers envision that stablecoins will also have an expanded reach in the payment system and be commonly used for everyday transactions, both domestic and cross-border.
rationale: Discusses potential future use cases of stablecoins, not CBDC design features.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: So it is important to have strong frameworks for the quality and sufficiency of reserves and risk management and governance.
rationale: Discusses general regulatory frameworks for stablecoins without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: As noted in a recent report on stablecoins by the President's Working Group on Financial Markets, it is important to guard against run risk, whereby the prospect of an issuer not being able to promptly and adequately meet redemption requests for the stablecoin at par could result in a sudden surge in redemption demand.
rationale: Discusses stablecoin run risk without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: It is also important to address settlement risk, whereby funds settlement is not certain and final when expected, and systemic risk, whereby the failure or distress of a stablecoin provider could adversely affect the broader financial system.
rationale: Discusses general risks (settlement, systemic) without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

rationale: Expresses skepticism about CBDC need but names no concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I am not a national security expert.
rationale: The sentence is a personal disclaimer about expertise, not a discussion of any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: But one area where economics, CBDCs, and national security dovetail is the role of the dollar.
rationale: Discusses the general relationship between CBDCs and dollar status without naming any specific design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Advocates for creating a U.S. CBDC often assert how it is important to the long-term status of the dollar, particularly if other major jurisdictions adopt a CBDC.
rationale: Discusses motivation for CBDC (dollar status, international competition) without naming any concrete design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I disagree.
rationale: The sentence expresses disagreement with a general claim about CBDC and dollar status but mentions no concrete design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: As I will discuss, the underlying reasons for why the dollar is the dominant currency have little to do with technology, and I believe the introduction of a CBDC would not affect those underlying reasons.
rationale: Discusses CBDC's effect on dollar dominance without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I offer this view, again, in the spirit of dialogue, knowing how important these issues are, and I am very happy to engage in vigorous debate regarding my view.
rationale: Meta-commentary about the speaker's openness to debate, no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I remain open to the arguments advanced by others in this space.
rationale: Expresses openness to debate with no concrete CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The Role of the U.S. Dollar After World War II and the creation of the Bretton Woods system, the U.S. dollar served as the central currency for the international monetary system.
rationale: Historical context about the dollar's role in Bretton Woods; no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Other countries agreed to keep the exchange value of their currencies fixed to the dollar, and eventually, countries came to settle international balances in dollars.
rationale: Historical description of dollar's international role with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: That role has continued long after the Bretton Woods system dissolved.
rationale: Discusses the dollar's historical role with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: By any measure, the dollar is the dominant global currency—for funding markets, foreign exchange transactions, and invoicing.
rationale: Describes the dollar's global role without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It also is the world's predominant reserve currency.
rationale: Discusses the dollar's reserve currency status, not any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In terms of the dollar's reserve currency status, 60 percent of disclosed official foreign reserves are held in dollars, far surpassing the shares of other currencies, with the majority of these dollar reserves held in safe and liquid U.S. Treasury securities.
rationale: Describes dollar's reserve currency status with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Even in a world of largely floating exchange rates, many countries either implicitly or explicitly anchor their currencies to the dollar; together, these countries account for about half of world gross domestic product.
rationale: Discusses dollar dominance in exchange rate anchoring with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The dollar is by far the dominant currency for international trade.
rationale: Discusses dollar's role in international trade with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Apart from intra-European trade, dollar invoicing is used in more than three-fourths of global trade, including 96 percent of trade in the Americas.
rationale: Describes dollar dominance in trade invoicing without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Approximately 60 percent of international and foreign currency liabilities—international banking loans and deposits as well as international debt securities—are denominated in dollars.
rationale: Describes dollar's role in international finance with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: And the dollar remains the single most widely used currency in foreign exchange transactions.
rationale: Describes dollar's role in foreign exchange markets without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Why does this matter to the United States?
rationale: This is a transitional question about motivation for caring about CBDC and dollar dominance, with no concrete design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: As indicated in the Board's CBDC discussion paper, the dollar's international role lowers transaction and borrowing costs for U.S. households, businesses, and government.
rationale: Discusses the dollar's international role and its benefits, not a specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It widens the pool of creditors and investors for U.S. investments.
rationale: Discusses general benefits of dollar's international role, not a specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It may insulate the U.S. economy from shocks from abroad.
rationale: Discusses general macro effects of dollar dominance, not a specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It also allows the United States to influence standards for the global monetary system.
rationale: Discusses general benefits of dollar's global role, not any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The dollar's role doesn't only benefit the United States.
rationale: Discusses the dollar's global role and benefits, not any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The dollar serves as a safe, stable, and dependable form of money around the world.
rationale: Describes the dollar's general role as money globally without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It serves as a reliable common denominator for global trade and a dependable settlement instrument for cross-border payments.
rationale: Describes the dollar's role in global trade and payments without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In the process, it reduces the cost of transferring capital and smooths the world of global payments, including for households and businesses outside of America.
rationale: Discusses general benefits of the dollar in global payments with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For example, consider the dollar's role in foreign exchange markets.
rationale: Introduces an example about the dollar's role in FX markets with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: To make a foreign exchange transaction between two lightly traded currencies, it is often less expensive to trade the first currency with the dollar, and then to trade the dollar with the second currency, rather than to trade the two currencies directly.
rationale: Describes dollar's role in FX markets with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The factors driving the dollar's role as a reserve currency are well researched and well demonstrated, including the depth and liquidity of U.S. financial markets, the size and openness of the U.S. economy, and international trust in U.S. institutions and the rule of law.
rationale: Discusses factors behind the dollar's reserve currency status, not any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: We must keep these factors in mind in any debate regarding the long-term importance of the dollar.
rationale: The sentence discusses factors affecting dollar dominance generally, with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: CBDCs and the U.S. Dollar Threats to the U.S. dollar's international dominance are numerous, including shifting geopolitical alliances and pressure to invoice in alternative currencies, as well as deeper and more open foreign financial markets.
rationale: Discusses general threats to dollar dominance without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: My focus today is on just one supposed threat—namely, the purported shifting payments landscape as a result of the growth of digital assets, particularly CBDCs.
rationale: Sentence discusses CBDCs as a general topic and potential threat to the dollar, with no specific design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Recent years have seen a number of changes to the payments system, from instant interbank payments to mobile payment services to a shift toward nonbank payment providers.
rationale: Describes general payments landscape changes without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Some of this shift has been through the rise in digital assets and include cryptocurrencies and other crypto-assets such as stablecoins, which have money-like characteristics.
rationale: Describes the general landscape of digital assets without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: They also include CBDCs.
rationale: Sentence merely states that CBDCs are included in the category of digital assets, with no concrete design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: A CBDC is a digital instrument that is a liability of the central bank.
rationale: Defines what a CBDC is (central bank liability) without naming any concrete design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: That is all it is—a direct liability of a central bank.
rationale: Direct liability implies unintermediated/direct issuance model, making CBDC a stronger deposit substitute.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: What major security gap exists that a CBDC, and only a CBDC, can close?
rationale: This is a rhetorical question about CBDC's general purpose or motivation, with no concrete design feature named.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: What would be the effect of CBDCs and other digital money-like instruments on the role of the dollar?
rationale: The sentence asks about CBDC's effect on the dollar's role without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: There are many ways to approach this question, but I want to do so by using a simple example: What is it about a CBDC that would make a non-U.S. company, engaging in international financial transactions, more or less likely to use the dollar?
rationale: The sentence poses a general question about CBDC's effect on dollar usage without naming any specific design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This example, of course, focuses on the reasons for why contracts are generally invoiced in U.S. dollars, which is just one feature of the dollar's international role.
rationale: The sentence clarifies the scope of the example (invoicing in dollars) without discussing any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: To me, however, it simplifies the overall question regarding the effect of a CBDC on the dollar's dominance.
rationale: The sentence discusses the analytical approach to studying CBDC effects on dollar dominance, not any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: We can break down this question into three others: First, would a foreign CBDC affect this non-U.S. company's decisions?
rationale: The sentence poses an analytical question about CBDC effects without naming any concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Second, would a U.S. CBDC affect them?
rationale: The sentence poses a hypothetical question about whether a U.S. CBDC would affect decisions, but does not discuss any concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: And, third, while stablecoins are not CBDCs, how would a privately issued stablecoin have a different effect?
rationale: The sentence poses a comparative question about stablecoins versus CBDCs without discussing any concrete CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Foreign CBDCs First, I will consider the emergence of one or more foreign CBDCs in a world with no U.S. CBDC.
rationale: Introduces a scenario about foreign CBDCs but mentions no concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: What would be the effect on the non-U.S. company?
rationale: The sentence poses a hypothetical question about effects on a company without discussing any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Let's assume the company acts pragmatically; it would only move away from using the U.S. dollar if it is better off by doing so.
rationale: Discusses hypothetical company behavior regarding dollar usage without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The discussion around this question usually tends to focus on the potential technological advantages of a CBDC and doesn't grapple with the underlying reasons for the dominance of the dollar.
rationale: Discusses what CBDC debates focus on (technology vs dollar dominance) without naming any specific design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: That is, advocates for a CBDC tend to promote the potential for a CBDC to reduce payment frictions by lowering transaction costs, enabling faster settlement speeds, and providing a better user experience.
rationale: Discusses general technological advantages and payment frictions without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I am highly skeptical that a CBDC on its own could sufficiently reduce the traditional payment frictions to prevent things like fraud, theft, money laundering, or the financing of terrorism.
rationale: Discusses general payment frictions and CBDC limitations without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Though CBDC systems may be able to automate a number of processes that, in part, address these challenges, they are not unique in doing so.
rationale: The sentence discusses CBDC capabilities in general (automation) without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Meaningful efforts are under way at the international level to improve cross-border payments in many ways, with the vast majority of these improvements coming not from CBDCs but improvements to existing payment systems.
rationale: Discusses improvements to cross-border payments generally without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For argument's sake, though, let's suppose that this foreign CBDC is more attractive for payments to the non-U.S. company, perhaps for technological reasons, or because the preferences of the firm's consumers or trading partners change in response to the introduction of the CBDC.
rationale: The sentence discusses hypothetical attractiveness of a foreign CBDC for payments without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Due to the well-known network effects in payments, the more users the foreign CBDC acquires, the greater will be the pressure on the non-U.S. company to also use the foreign CBDC.
rationale: Discusses network effects and adoption dynamics of foreign CBDC without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In this case, it is true that the appeal of the foreign CBDC as a transactions medium—not as a unit account or store of value—might gain at the expense of the dollar.
rationale: Discusses CBDC's competitive effect on the dollar as a transactions medium without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: These effects will likely only be on the margin because they rely on a large enough number of individuals and businesses being nearly indifferent between the dollar and the foreign currency in CBDC form.
rationale: Discusses marginal effects of foreign CBDC adoption without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: But the broader factors underpinning the dollar's international role would not change.
rationale: Discusses geopolitical factors underpinning dollar dominance, not any concrete CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Changing those factors would require large geopolitical shifts separate from CBDC issuance, including greater availability of attractive safe assets and liquid financial markets in other jurisdictions that are at least on par with, if not better than, those that exist in the United States.
rationale: Discusses geopolitical and macroeconomic factors affecting dollar dominance, not any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The factors supporting the primacy of the dollar are not technological, but include the ample supply and liquid market for U.S. Treasury securities and other debt and the long-standing stability of the U.S. economy and political system.
rationale: Discusses general factors supporting dollar primacy without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: No other country is fully comparable with the United States on those fronts, and a CBDC would not change that.
rationale: Discusses general CBDC effects on dollar primacy without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Finally, as I've noted before, it is possible that a foreign-issued CBDC could have the opposite of its intended effect and make companies even less willing to use that country's currency.
rationale: Discusses potential macro effects of foreign CBDCs on currency usage without naming any specific design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Since digital currencies would make it easier for a government to monitor transactions, shifting to a CBDC might make a company less willing to use that country's currency.
rationale: Mentions monitoring capability as a design feature but discusses its effect on currency adoption, not deposit substitution.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For example, I suspect that many companies will remain wary of China's CBDC for just this reason.
rationale: The sentence discusses adoption concerns about China's CBDC due to surveillance, not a specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: U.S. CBDC I am also skeptical that a U.S. CBDC would affect this hypothetical foreign company's decisionmaking.
rationale: Sentence expresses skepticism about CBDC's general effects on company decision-making without naming any specific design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: A U.S. CBDC is unlikely to dramatically reshape the liquidity or depth of U.S. capital markets.
rationale: Discusses general macro effects of CBDC on capital markets without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It is unlikely to affect the openness of the U.S. economy, reconfigure trust in U.S. institutions, or deepen America's commitment to the rule of law.
rationale: Discusses general effects of CBDC on institutions and economy without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: As I have said before, the introduction of a U.S. CBDC would come with a number of costs and risks, including cyber risk and the threat of disintermediating commercial banks, both of which could harm, rather than help, the U.S. dollar's standing internationally.
rationale: Discusses general costs and risks of CBDC including disintermediation threat, but names no specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Like a foreign CBDC, the technological advantages of a U.S. CBDC would have a hard time overcoming long-standing payments frictions without violating international financial integrity standards.
rationale: Discusses general technological advantages and compliance constraints without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For the non-U.S. company already conducting its business in dollars, introducing a U.S. CBDC would not provide material benefits over and above the current reasons for making U.S. dollar-denominated payments.
rationale: Discusses general benefits of CBDC versus existing payment options without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For non-U.S. companies conducting their business in currencies other than dollars, a U.S. CBDC similarly would likely not be preferred to their current options.
rationale: Discusses general adoption and preferences for U.S. CBDC by non-U.S. entities without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It could be that individuals outside the United States would find a U.S. CBDC particularly attractive, but, again, making a U.S. CBDC globally available would raise a number of issues, including money laundering and international financial stability concerns.
rationale: Restricting global availability (limiting access to non-U.S. individuals) is a protective design feature that reduces CBDC's reach as a deposit substitute.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: And as with a foreign-issued CBDC, the dollar's function as a unit of account and store of value is unlikely to be affected, resulting in a limited effect on the international role of the dollar.
rationale: Discusses macro effects on dollar's international role without naming any concrete CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Stablecoins The last scenario I want to consider is one in which a privately issued stablecoin pegged to a sovereign currency is available for international payments.
rationale: Introduces stablecoins as a scenario topic without discussing any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Stablecoins are crypto-assets that aim to maintain a stable value relative to a specified asset or pool of assets.
rationale: This sentence defines stablecoins generically without discussing any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The reasons that stablecoins may be more attractive than existing options for payments include their ability to provide real-time payments at lower cost between countries that were previously poorly serviced and to provide a safe store of value for individuals residing in or transacting with countries with weak economic fundamentals.
rationale: Discusses stablecoin advantages for payments and store of value without naming any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This is different than an intermediated U.S. CBDC, for which access in developing economies would depend on banks' incentives to provide such access.
rationale: The intermediated model limits CBDC's reach compared to stablecoins, protecting banks' deposit base from direct competition.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Stablecoins, however, may be held directly in any country that allows its citizens to do so.
rationale: Discusses stablecoin access generally without naming any specific CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: To improve payments, especially for jurisdictions that are not well served under the current global payments ecosystem, stablecoins must be risk-managed and subject to a robust supervisory and regulatory framework.
rationale: Discusses regulatory framework for stablecoins, not a specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could such an asset affect the role of the U.S. dollar?
rationale: The sentence poses a question about the dollar's role without discussing any concrete CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Once again, I am unsure whether even a large issuance of a stablecoin could have anything more than a marginal effect.
rationale: Discusses potential effects of stablecoin issuance without naming any concrete CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It has often been suggested by commentators that private money-like instruments such as stablecoins threaten the effectiveness of monetary policy.
rationale: Discusses stablecoins' potential effect on monetary policy without naming any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I don't believe that to be the case, and it should be noted that nearly all the major stablecoins to date are denominated in dollars, and therefore U.S. monetary policy should affect the decision to hold stablecoins similar to the decision to hold currency.
rationale: Discusses monetary policy effects of stablecoins without naming any concrete CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This follows from a vast body of evidence in international economics showing how countries pegging their exchange rates effectively import monetary policy from the country to which their currency is pegged.
rationale: Discusses international monetary economics and exchange rate pegging with no mention of any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Also, because stablecoins are pegged to the dollar, they may increase rather than reduce the primacy of the dollar abroad, since demand for stablecoins increases demand for dollar-denominated reserve assets held by the stablecoin issuer.
rationale: Discusses stablecoins and dollar demand, not any concrete CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Conclusion The ongoing debate over the risks and benefits of a CBDC is important, and I am happy to continue to engage with both advocates and skeptics of CBDCs.
rationale: This is a meta-statement about engaging in the CBDC debate with no concrete design feature mentioned.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: But, for the reasons I have laid out, I don't think there are implications here for the role of the United States in the global economy and financial system.
rationale: Discusses implications for US global role, not any concrete CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: We should instead focus and debate the salient CBDC-related topics, like its effects on financial stability, payment system improvements, and financial inclusion.
rationale: Lists general CBDC topics (financial stability, payments, inclusion) without naming any concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Thank you again for having me to participate in this fantastic event.
rationale: Closing pleasantry with no CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: It is a pleasure to be with you today to discuss the evolving money and payments landscape in the United States, which is a topic of primary importance to the Federal Reserve.
rationale: Introductory statement about the topic with no concrete CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: Technological innovation has changed this landscape in recent years, as we have seen the emergence of new financial services entrants offering payments services, new platforms designed to increase the speed of payments, clearing, and settlement, and new forms of digital money.
rationale: Describes general technological changes in payments landscape without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: Over the past several years, and as a direct result of these developments, we have seen a significant increase in attention on central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) from central banks around the world in addition to a great deal of international and domestic engagement on CBDC.
rationale: The sentence discusses increased attention on CBDCs globally without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: A number of central banks have taken steps to begin exploring the potential uses of a CBDC in their home countries.
rationale: The sentence describes central banks exploring CBDC generally without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: A very small number have adopted a CBDC for their local jurisdictions.
rationale: The sentence describes CBDC adoption status without mentioning any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: And of course, discussions of the purpose, design, and potential risks of a U.S. CBDC, and technical research about key design elements, continue here in the United States.
rationale: The sentence mentions design as a topic of discussion but does not specify any concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: While the Federal Reserve plays an important role in these ongoing discussions and technical research, the Fed would not implement a U.S. CBDC without the approval of Congress.
rationale: Discusses governance and authorization requirements for CBDC implementation, not any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: In broad terms, a CBDC is simply a new form of digital liability of a central bank.
rationale: Definitional statement about what CBDC is, with no concrete design feature or parameter mentioned.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: Because it is issued by a central bank, CBDC is typically thought of as being denominated in the currency of that central bank.
rationale: Describes general definitional property of CBDC denomination without naming any concrete design feature.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: One could imagine a digital U.S. dollar, a digital euro, or a digital pound.
rationale: Sentence only illustrates currency denomination examples without discussing any concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: Beyond this baseline definition though, "what is a CBDC" defies a simple definition.
rationale: Sentence states CBDC lacks simple definition but names no concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: A CBDC built on distributed ledger technology offers a wide range of design and potential use options, as well as potential risks.
rationale: Mentions design options exist but does not specify any concrete feature or its deposit-substitution implications.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: This variability complicates any discussion of a CBDC simply because we may not be talking about the same thing.
rationale: The sentence discusses the complexity of CBDC discourse due to design variability but does not name any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: There are two threshold questions that a policymaker needs to ask before any decision to move forward with a CBDC.
rationale: Discusses the decision-making process for CBDC without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: First, what problem is the policymaker trying to solve, and is a CBDC a potential solution?
rationale: The sentence poses a general question about CBDC motivation and problem-solving without naming any concrete design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: Second, what features and considerations--including unintended consequences--may a policymaker want to consider in deciding to design and adopt a CBDC?
rationale: Lists design features and considerations as questions to explore, without endorsing limiting or expanding choices.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: While it would be impossible for me to provide a comprehensive analysis of every issue surrounding CBDC, my goal today is to offer a perspective on these two threshold questions and to conclude with some thoughts about the imperative for future research on CBDCs and the potential future of CBDCs in the United States.
rationale: The sentence is a meta-statement about the speech's scope and structure, with no concrete CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: What Problem Could a CBDC Solve?
rationale: This is a section heading posing a general question about CBDC motivation, not discussing any concrete design feature.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: In my view, the fundamental question is: what problem could a CBDC solve?
rationale: The sentence poses a general question about CBDC's purpose without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: CBDC and the Payment System One issue being examined is whether a CBDC or even broader forms of digital money could make the payment system more efficient.
rationale: Discusses potential benefits of CBDC for payment efficiency without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: Do these new technologies present opportunities to increase the speed of payments and/or lower costs and frictions within the payment system?
rationale: The sentence poses a general question about CBDC's potential payment system benefits without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: Of course, this question takes place in the context of the payments infrastructure in each jurisdiction, both for domestic payments and for cross-border payments.
rationale: The sentence discusses the context for evaluating payment technologies without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: Many countries have launched faster payment systems and continue to investigate how central banks can support these payment systems.
rationale: Discusses faster payment systems and central bank support generally, with no specific CBDC design feature or parameter mentioned.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: We have seen a wide range of motivations for this work, including addressing specific inefficiencies in the payment system, providing a CBDC if cash use were to decline, or promoting broader private-sector innovation for future generations of payments.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: In the United States, beginning later this year, the Federal Reserve's FedNowSM Service will enable banks in the United States to offer their customers the ability to send and receive payments in real-time.
rationale: Discusses FedNow as an alternative payment system, not a CBDC design feature.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: Policymakers have also raised other arguments for why a CBDC may be suitable in their home countries.
rationale: The sentence discusses motivations for CBDC in general without naming any specific design feature or parameter.

speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
sentence: Some have argued that a CBDC would facilitate large-value transactions between financial institutions.
rationale: Describes a potential use case (large-value transactions) without naming any concrete design feature or parameter.

sentence: But Bitcoin and some other early iterations of cryptocurrencies have exhibited extreme volatility, limited throughput capacity, unpredictable transaction costs, limited or no governance, and limited transparency, which have limited their utility as a means of payment and unit of account.
rationale: Discusses limitations of cryptocurrencies, not CBDC design features.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Stablecoins were designed specifically to overcome the substantial volatility exhibited by first-generation cryptocurrencies, which limits their reach in payments and their utility as a unit of account.
rationale: Discusses stablecoin motivation and general purpose, not a specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: As the name implies, stablecoins aim to maintain stable value by tying the digital currency to an asset or basket of assets, such as commercial bank deposits or government-issued bonds.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Stablecoins also differ from the initial set of cryptocurrencies in that they may be issued by a central entity and rely on third-party institutions for some aspects.
rationale: Describes stablecoin organizational structure, not CBDC design features affecting deposit substitution.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Just as any currency's value as a medium of exchange increases with the size of the network using it, so too the power of a stablecoin payment system will depend on its ability to achieve widespread adoption, due to the associated network externalities.
rationale: Discusses network effects and adoption dynamics of stablecoins generally, with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In light of the 2.7 billion active monthly users on Facebook's platforms, the Libra stablecoin project stands out for the speed with which its network could reach global scale in a payment system.
rationale: Discusses network scale and adoption potential, not a concrete CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: To assess the efforts by stablecoin issuers to provide the three functions of money, it is useful first to consider existing arrangements for the issuance, regulation, and transfer of money.
rationale: The sentence discusses a framework for assessing stablecoins generally, not any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Central bank money and commercial bank money are the foundations of the modern financial system.
rationale: Describes the general role of central bank and commercial bank money without mentioning any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Central bank money is composed of physical cash and money held in deposits at a central bank.
rationale: Describes what central bank money is, not a CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Central bank money is important for payment systems because it represents a safe settlement asset, allowing users to exchange central bank liabilities with confidence in their acceptance and reliability.
rationale: Describes the general role of central bank money in payment systems without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In addition, central banks can play a critical role as providers of liquidity by lending central bank money at moments of stress.
rationale: Describes central bank's general liquidity provision role without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Commercial bank money refers to money held in deposits at commercial banks.
rationale: Defines commercial bank money without discussing any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: It is widely used in part because people are confident that they can convert it on demand to the liability of another commercial bank or the central bank, such as physical cash.
rationale: Describes convertibility of existing commercial bank deposits to cash, not a CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: This confidence comes in no small part because bank deposits are insured, and commercial banks are subject to supervision, regulation, and deposit insurance requirements.
rationale: Discusses existing bank deposit system features (insurance, regulation) without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Consumers and businesses also use this money in transactions because of its convenience and availability, which in turn expand with the size of the network using this money.
rationale: Describes network effects and convenience of money in general without naming any specific CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Nonbank private money or assets can also facilitate transactions among a network of users.
rationale: Describes private money/assets generally without naming any CBDC design feature or parameter.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In some cases, such as airline miles, such assets may have value only within the network.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In other cases, the issuer of an asset within a network may guarantee convertibility to a sovereign currency.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Consumers trust that the company issuing such money will be able to honor these liabilities.
rationale: Discusses consumer trust in private money issuers generally, with no specific CBDC design feature mentioned.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Many U.S. consumers have experience with nonbank private money in the form of gift cards, loyalty points, and virtual gaming currencies.
rationale: Describes existing nonbank private money examples without discussing any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Although many of these are relatively limited in scale and purpose, some nonbank money networks are sizeable.
rationale: Describes scale of existing nonbank money networks without mentioning any CBDC design feature.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Starbucks reported that it had $1.6 billion in stored value card liabilities as of September 2018—more than the deposits held at many depository institutions.
